$comment: MIDI note number -> key contact, for the hardware-key parser (#351), pinned for all three
MidiKeyParser.paddleForNote in android/.../morsekit/MidiKeyMessage.kt and the desktop copy.
Read by ios/Sources/MorseKitCheck/main.swift and MidiKeyNotesFixtureTest.kt (android, desktop).
Sources, not captured from either port. Vail Adapter (Vail-CW/vail-adapter
docs/MIDI_INTEGRATION_SPEC.md): note 0 is the straight key and every element its keyer modes
send, already timed; notes 1 (dit) and 2 (dah) are raw paddle contacts sent only in
Passthrough, where the host does the timing. N6ARA TinyMIDI (the Vail web client's
inputs.mjs treats 1/2/20/21 as raw paddles): raw dit 20, dah 21. Morserino-32 Pocket
'USB Output = MIDI', oe1wkl/Morserino-32 PR #224 (merged 2026-10-29): channel 1, raw dit 20,
dah 21 (Lynovation CTR2-MIDI convention), and note 30 for the straight key, sent only with
the Pocket's keyer set to Straight Key mode; unverified on real Pocket hardware. Notes 61 and
62 are mappings the parsers had before this fixture; no device source for them was found
(they are in neither the Vail spec nor its web client), so they pin existing behaviour only.
'mapped' lists every note that keys; 'unmapped' lists notes that must stay silent because the
app listens to every MIDI source and an unrelated synth must never register as keying (the
neighbours of each mapped note, middle C, and the extremes). A note moving between the lists
is a behaviour change: say so in the commit. Do not regenerate to make a failing test pass.
